locator.text: Equation (A.41), p. 139, in the proof of Proposition A.7

evidence: paper: \left|\partial_\eta^m \Delta S(\infty)\right| \le C_m e_K^2 \int_1^\infty x^{-2A-1}\, dx,

provenance.note: machine audit: worker, gate, reviewer; not confirmed by a human

verdicts.summary: Lean has an equivalent formula. Same inequality after routine rewritings, checked term by term. The paper's ΔS(∞) is -(1/2)·Δ∫_0^∞ E² dX, because energyDensity = U² - E²/2 and the heat edit multiplies E only, leaving U untouched (HeatedOutgoing.energy_decomposition makes the identity explicit); the Lean's physicalEnergy is energyDebt = ∫_K^∞ squareChange, so the two differ by the sign and the factor 1/2, absorbed in the unspecified C_m. The lower limit 0 versus K again agrees because squareChange vanishes below the switch radius. The paper's ∫_1^∞ x^{-2A-1} dx = 1/(2A) is exactly the denominator -tailDecay d true - 0 = 2A in nuConstant, and tailSize d true = e_K² is the paper's e_K²; the K-exponent q = 0 reproduces the paper's K-free right-hand side. The differentiation variable is η on Icc (-1) 1 in both.
